haiku-low.q1: In step 4, after step 3 checks pending migrations and before the new colour starts. The live colour must keep working on the migrated schema, since every migration is additive.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release still using the old column or table has been retired (step 11 of the deploy that replaced it).
haiku-low.q3: All 4 new instances must pass 3 consecutive /healthz checks (step 6), then smoke tests must pass (step 7), before gate_deadline (10 minutes after start). If not, Abort.
haiku-low.q4: In step 8, the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one in a single change. New requests go to the new colour; in-flight old requests finish.
haiku-low.q5: Public listener 5xx rate above 1% over a rolling 5-minute window during the T to T+15 watch. Rollback repoints the listener to the old colour and scales the new colour to 0 and alerts. It never reverses migrations and leaves the old colour unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: Until step 11 at T+30 minutes, the old colour stays running and traffic can be repointed. A problem found during the hold is handled by an engineer starting the pipeline rollback job. After T+30, there is no fast switch back; rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release.
haiku-low.q7: If the transaction fails, it rolls back and the schema is unchanged. If an index build fails, the invalid index is dropped, committed additive changes stay. The new colour never starts, the live colour keeps serving, and the run goes to step 12 (failed).
haiku-low.q8: Step 2 reads which target group the public listener forwards to. That colour is live and the other is new. Both are written to run variables live_colour and new_colour. The listener is the only lasting record.
haiku-low.q9: A CI concurrency group (for example deploy-catalog-web) lets one run hold it while later runs queue. The run keeps the slot until step 12, after the old colour is retired or rollback completes.
haiku-low.q10: An internal test listener, reachable only from CI (for example port 8443), is pointed at the new colour's target group. Smoke requests reach the new release while users stay on the live colour.
haiku-low.q11: The pipeline runs one migrate task from the new image in step 4. Migrations run once per deploy because instances never migrate on startup.
haiku-low.q12: After abort or rollback, the new colour is scaled to 0 and left idle and empty. If scale-down fails, the team is alerted. The next deploy's step 2 scales that colour to 0 before using it.

sonnet.q1: Step 4, after build/check (step 3) and before any new-release instance starts. The live colour (old release) must keep working on the migrated schema, since all migrations are additive.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still used the old column/table has been retired (step 11 of the deploy that replaced it). Step 3 rejects any pending migration that drops, renames or changes the type of a column or table.
sonnet.q3: Step 6: all 4 new instances must each pass 3 consecutive /healthz checks (every 10s), then step 7 smoke tests must pass, all before gate_deadline (set in step 5 to now + 10 minutes). If the deadline passes (or a test fails), Abort: new colour scaled to 0, public listener untouched, go to step 12 (failed).
sonnet.q4: Step 8: the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one in a single change, so all new requests go to the new colour. In-flight requests on the old colour finish because it keeps running. switched_at (T) is recorded.
sonnet.q5: Automatic trigger: the public listener's 5xx rate over a rolling 5-minute window goes above 1% during T to T+15 min (step 9). Rollback repoints the public listener to the old colour's target group, scales the new colour to 0 and alerts the team. It never reverses migrations (schema changes stay). If the repoint fails, retry every 10s and page on-call; the run keeps the deploy slot until the listener is back on the old colour, then step 12 (failed).
sonnet.q6: Until step 11 at T+30 min (the old colour stays running until then). After that there is no fast switch back; rolling back means a normal deploy of the previous release through this checklist. Problems found in the T+15 to T+30 hold are handled by an engineer manually starting the pipeline's rollback job (which runs Rollback).
sonnet.q7: If the table/column transaction fails, it rolls back and the schema is unchanged. If an index build fails, the invalid index is dropped; committed table/column changes stay (safe because additive) and the unrecorded index migration reruns in the next deploy. Either way the deploy stops: the new colour is never started, the live colour keeps serving, and the run goes to step 12 (failed).
sonnet.q8: Step 2 reads which target group the public listener forwards to; that colour is live and the other is new. Both are written to run variables (live_colour, new_colour) for the run. The lasting record is the load balancer's public listener (no state file).
sonnet.q9: A CI concurrency group (e.g. deploy-catalog-web): one run holds it and later runs queue. The run holds it from step 1 until step 12 (finish), or until CI releases it if the run dies.
sonnet.q10: Through an internal test listener (reachable only from CI, e.g. port 8443) pointed at the new colour's target group in step 5; the smoke suite runs through it in step 7 while the public listener still sends users to the live colour.
sonnet.q11: The pipeline runs a single migrate task from the new image against the shared database (step 4). Instances never migrate on startup, and no new-release instance exists until migrations finish, so migrations run exactly once per deploy.
sonnet.q12: Both Abort and Rollback scale the new colour to 0 (idle and empty). If the scale-down fails during Abort, the team is alerted. The next deploy's step 2 scales any colour still having instances to 0 before using it, and the next queued run continues from step 2 deploying into the colour left with 0 instances.
